body.p: Upon entry of this amendment, claims 1, 4-8, 10-16, and 23-29 are pending. Claims 1, 4- 8, 10, 13, 14, 16, 23, and 25-28 are amended, claims 11, and 24 are in the original form, claims 3 and 15 are cancelled, and claims 74 and 75 are added. Support for the amendments can be found throughout the application as filed, including at least in paragraphs [0081]-[0088] and the originally-filed claims. No new matter is added by this amendment. This Amendment is being made solely to expedite prosecution of this application and does not constitute an acquiescence to any prior art or rejections identified by the Office.

The Office rejects claims 1, 3-8, 10-16, and 23-28 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the Applicant regards as the invention.

Although Applicant does not necessarily agree with the Office, to expedite allowance of this Application, Applicant has made clarifying amendments to claims 1, 4-8, 10, 13, 14, 16, 23, and 25-28 and cancelled claims 3 and 15. Applicant respectfully requests the Office to reconsider and allow all pending claims.

Claims 1, 3-8, 10-16, and 23-28 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as allegedly being rendered obvious by US 2012/0265037 to Bohm et al. ("Bohm") in view of US 2011/0021889 to Hoss et al. ("Hoss"). See Office Action at 4. Although Applicant does not necessarily agree with
the Office, to expedite allowance of this Application, Applicant has made clarifying amendments
to claims 1, 4-8, 10, 13, 14, 16, 23, and 25-28 to further clarify the distinction between the
claims and the cited art.
Independent claim 1 of this Application, as amended, recites:
1. A method of adjusting analyte sensor data, comprising:
storing, by processing circuitry, at least one parameter including a slope
associated with a sensitivity of an analyte sensor;
collecting, by the processing circuity, sensor data from the analyte sensor
when the analyte sensor is at least partially inserted into interstitial fluid of a user, the sensor data including data indicative of a level of an analyte in the interstitial
fluid;
obtaining, by the processing circuitry, a shelf start time from an electronic
memory communicatively coupled with the processing circuitry;
determining, by the processing circuitry, a shelf duration of the analyte
sensor based on the shelf start time;
adjusting, by the processing circuitry, processing of the sensor data to
compensate for the shelf duration, the adjusting comprising adjusting the slope
associated with the sensitivity of the analyte sensor;
determining, by the processing circuitry, the level of the analyte of the
user from the sensor data using the adjusted slope; and
outputting the determined level of the analyte to a display.
Even if the proposed Bohm-Hoss combination were proper, it would still fail to disclose,
teach, or suggest all of the limitations of independent claim 1.
As an example, the proposed Bohm-Hoss combination fails to disclose, teach, or suggest
"obtaining, by the processing circuitry, a shelf start time from an electronic memory
communicatively coupled with the processing circuitry;" and "determining, by the processing
circuitry, a shelf duration of the analyte sensor based on the shelf start time", as independent
claim 1 recites. The Office Action cites to paragraph 0406 of Bohm as allegedly disclosing the
shelf duration as claimed. Bohm, however, merely describes calibration process 2400 can use

one or more pre-implant information 2402, including time since sensor manufacture. See Bohm, paragraphs [0398]-[0407]. Bohm does not elaborate or explain how the "time since sensor manufacture" is determined and particularly fails to disclose obtaining a shelf start time for the analyte sensor from an electronic memory and affirmatively determining the shelf duration based on the shelf start time prior to adjusting processing of sensor data to compensate for the shelf duration. Hoss does not make up for the deficiencies of Bohm, either alone or in combination, and the Office does not assert otherwise. Consequently, the proposed Bohm-Hoss combination fails to disclose, teach, or suggest "obtaining, by the processing circuitry, a shelf start time from an electronic memory communicatively coupled with the processing circuitry;" and "determining, by the processing circuitry, a shelf duration of the analyte sensor based on the shelf start time."

The Office may not disregard specific recitations of Applicant's claims to maintain a rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 103. According to the M.P.E.P., "[a]ll words in a claim must be considered in judging the patentability of that claim against the prior art." M.P.E.P. § 2143.03 (citations omitted). Moreover, "[w]hen evaluating claims for obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103, all the limitations of the claims must be considered and given weight." Id. (emphasis added). As shown above, even assuming for the sake of argument the proposed Bohm-Hoss combination were proper, the proposed Bohm-Hoss combination would still fail to disclose, teach, or suggest all the limitations of independent claim 1. Therefore, the proposed Bohm-Hoss combination does not render independent claim 1 obvious.

For at least these reasons, independent claim 1 is allowable over the proposed Bohm-Hoss combination. Applicant respectfully requests the Office to reconsider and allow this independent claim and all its dependent claims.

Claims 4-8, 10-14, 16, 23-28, and 74 depend, directly or indirectly, from independent claim 1. Applicant, therefore, respectfully submits that claims 4-8, 10-14, 16, 23-28, and 74 are allowable at least based on their dependence from allowable independent claim 1. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejections of claims 4-8, 10-14, 16, 23-28, and 74 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 be withdrawn.

Applicant submits that this application is in condition for allowance at least for the reasons set forth herein. If this application is not considered to be in condition for allowance by the Office, Applicant requests an interview with the Examiner to discuss this application. Applicant's Attorney Keith M. Jurek may be reached at telephone number (650) 739-7566 to schedule a mutually convenient date and time and to provide assistance or additional information as required.

Applicant submits that this Amendment and the accompanying remarks raise minimal new issues for consideration and do not necessitate the undertaking of an additional search of the art by the Office. This Amendment should therefore allow for immediate action by the Office, and for any additional consideration or search to be performed under the After Final Consideration Pilot Program 2.0.

On the basis of the foregoing remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that the pending claims of this application are allowable over the art of record. Applicant thus respectfully requests the previous rejections be withdrawn, and that the pending claims be allowed by the Office. Favorable consideration and timely allowance of this application are respectfully requested.

The above remarks are made solely to expedite prosecution of this application and do not constitute an acquiescence to any reference identified or rejection raised by the Office Action. Applicant believes that a full and complete reply has been made to the outstanding Office Action and, as such, the present application is in condition for allowance. Applicant thus respectfully requests the previous rejections be withdrawn, and that the pending claims be allowed by the Office. Favorable consideration and timely allowance of this application are respectfully requested.
